thread.title: 7 Key Ways To Check If The Stock Market Is Healthy

author: NANCY GONDO
title: 7 Key Ways To Check If The Stock Market Is Healthy
text:
Key index funds fell in the stock market today after the Federal Reserve hiked its key interest rate and signaled two more rate hikes this year.
X That weighed on the Dow industrials, sending SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) down 0.4% Wednesday. The ETF has been shaping a flat base with a potential buy point at 266.03. The biggest losers included Verizon Communications ( VZ ), Boeing ( BA ) and Caterpillar ( CAT ), which fell a respective 2.9%, 1.8% and 1.8%.
Only seven of the Dow's 30 stocks bucked the decline. But that underscores the beauty of owning an index fund, instead of an individual stock. Because several blue chips are up and others' declines aren't as steep, DIA is down 0.4% instead of 2.9% for Verizon.
An exchange traded fund offers a simple, low-cost and tax-efficient way to invest. It also lowers individual-stock risk, since you're buying a basket of stocks. ETFs trade just like stocks.
Today there are some 2,000 ETFs to choose from across a wide range of categories that cover stocks, bonds, commodities and currencies. And you can further slice and dice based on your preferences, whether you favor growth or value, small cap or midcap, tech or health care, or a specific country or region.
Choices Aplenty Below are some key index funds often used as a barometer to find out what's going on in the stock market for some of those segments.
Let's start with one of the most widely used bellwethers to track Wall Street's health:
DIA, with $22.1 billion in assets. The Dow is a price-weighted average of 30 blue chip stocks such as Apple ( AAPL ), General Electric ( GE ) and McDonald's ( MCD ). Many of these are your grandfather's stocks — they have a large market cap, are actively traded and tend to generate steady earnings growth.
